consensus_summary: Consensus primary meaning is God's final eschatological judgment through Christ: evaluation of all people/deeds, verdict separating righteous from wicked (throne, books, harvest, sheep/goats), affirmed creedal across traditions; common alternatives include historical/temporal judgments, realized/present judgment, purifying discipline, vindication of the oppressed, and human moral/church discernment.
book_summary: Judgment is the act of governing, administering, and discerning right from wrong, and also the ruling made or executed; condemnation is only one aspect, and good judgment follows God's law and statutes.
consensus_core_identification: Divine (especially final eschatological) evaluation and just verdict that separates/vindicates or condemns.
book_core_identification: Governing/administering and discerning right from wrong, plus the ruling executed, ordered by God's law (condemnation only one aspect).
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers primary reference on the Last Judgment (and closely related divine verdicts); the book centers general governance, administration, and law-shaped discernment, demoting condemnation and omitting eschatological finality as the defining frame.
material_contradiction: None; the book does not deny final or divine judgment, but re-scopes the term so eschatological condemnation is no longer the core identification.
rationale: Minimum cores share the justice/verdict family, so this is not replacement of the referent. Consensus locks the primary core on eschatological divine evaluation-and-separation; the book keeps judgment as ruling/discernment under God's law but broadens it to ongoing governing/administering and explicitly treats condemnation as only one aspect. That is a material boundary/extension change (REFINED + BOOK_BROADENS / BOOK_SUPERSET), not MATCH or full DIVERGENT contradiction. Listed consensus alternatives (discipline, vindication, moral discernment, historical justice) overlap some book cases but do not make the book's non-eschatological governance definition the settled primary consensus.
strongest_objection: The creedal, cross-traditional primary sense is the final judgment of the living and the dead, which the book entry never identifies.
